chapter_theme: The first half of Subramaniar Njanam tells a myth and turns it into method. Sound born of the Supreme becomes Siva, Shakti, the sevenfold creation, and Ganapati and Shanmuga; the mango is offered to whichever son circles the hill, Murugan rides round the world while Ganapati circles his parents' feet and wins; Murugan is consoled, goes to Kailasa, and at the Himalayan sages' plea destroys the asuras with the vel. Agastya then comes as disciple and asks the inner cause of the outer act; Murugan performs a fire rite, consecrates him from the filled pot, and teaches: the breath fixed at the tongue-tip opens the door of true knowledge; inhale at the root with VANG, let out in samadhi with SING; the seed letters OM RING ANG UNG, the five letters reversed head to foot, strings of bija syllables for the adharas, sacred ash, and pranayama that drives off the diseases called Death. Rite and legend are kept, but as the gross of which the breath is the subtle.
structure_note: 2486 to 2495 are narrative: creation, the mango contest, Murugan's circuit and the asura war. 2496 to 2500 bring Agastya as disciple, his question, the fire rite and the consecration. 2501 to 2510 are teaching: the breath with its syllables (2501), the seed letters and Om Namasivaya (2502), permutations of the five letters (2503, 2504), bija strings for the adharas (2505 to 2508), and pranayama against Death (2509, 2510).

2486.reading: In the beginning the sound born of the Supreme became Parasiva, formless-with-form; as the place of Siva called light it became Shakti; in the old world it became the sevenfold creation; standing as itself by the knowledge called order it became the full partless one; and by the grace of Shakti and Siva, Shanmuga and Ganapati came to be.
2486.nuance: Creation is traced from sound (சத்தம்), as in Tirumular's nada, and the two sons are the last and most concrete stage. எழுவகைத் தோற்றம் is the seven kinds of birth. சாதியென்ற is a rhyme-word whose sense here ('kind', 'gentle') is loose.

2487.reading: When Shakti and Siva stood as one, ripe within and full, they took the mango in hand, looked kindly at Kumaran and Ganapati, and said they would give the good fruit to the one who came round the hill; Kumaran, knowing the fruit's worth, leapt on his peacock and went round the hill.
2487.nuance: The mango legend is told without comment; its moral, that the inner circuit beats the outer, is left to the next verse. The fruit is the first of several objects in the work (pot, ash, nectar) that stand for what the practice yields.

2488.reading: After he had gone, Ganapati reflected that the firm Meru hill is they themselves; the moment he saw this he went round the feet of Siva and Uma with intent, took the fruit, meditated on them, and knowing the sign and praising the holy within the path, he ate and knew its taste; as he stood there they called the firm Ganapati to come.
2488.nuance: நீர் தாம் (you yourselves) resolves the contest: the mountain to be circled is the parents' feet. The verse adds meditation and 'knowing the sign' to the circuit, so that Ganapati's win is an act of knowledge, not of speed.

2489.reading: Saying 'come', they lifted and embraced him, gave him the milk of grace, made him the seat for the great five, king of the root, the first that is life to the five letters, pure being-consciousness, the first guru and teacher risen gathered, and told him to dwell within the flower of a thousand and eight petals, abiding by the mind's knowledge.
2489.nuance: மூலம் (root) is Ganapati's traditional seat, the muladhara; ஆயிரத்தெண் மலர் is the thousand-petalled lotus of the crown with eight added, an unexplained count. ஐவர் (the five) may be the five elements, the five gods or the five senses. The verse moves Ganapati from the legend into the body.

2490.reading: At the moment they said 'dwell and live', the solitary peacock-hero came before them; seeing the state in which he stood as rare tapas, they said 'precious jewel of our eye, come', with sorrow gave him one mango too, and bade him circle the great cosmic bounds, be reformed, gain long life, and live firmly as king of the hill.
2490.nuance: Murugan's loss becomes a commission: the circuit of the cosmos he already made is now his task, and மலைக்கரசு (king of the hill) is the Palani of the legend. The verse does not name Palani.

2491.reading: Told to live, the peacock-hero took the great feet of Siva-Shakti upon him, mounted the peacock and eagerly circled Kailasa; as he circled, the pure-minded ascetics on the north side of the Himalaya saw him and bowed at his feet, and as they stood in reverence the ascetics and rishis came up.

2492.reading: Looking at those who came and stood at the hill and bowed to him as great satguru, they said: on this hill-slope we have long lived in joy doing tapas, sir, but rakshasas come through the sky, wreck everything and chase us; stay here in beauty and guard our tapas; and with pure minds they began their tapas.
2492.nuance: The sages call Murugan சற்குரு before he has taught anything; the work's second half makes the title literal. Tradition reads the asuras who break tapas as the senses and thoughts; the verse itself tells only the story.

2493.reading: As they began, subduing the mind and guarding their state, standing pure and at play, he saw the audacity of the asuras whose minds would not be subdued, who made trouble without fear; firmly he mounted the peacock, took the red vel, meditated on its point so that the reddened asura kin should die, and loosed it, and the asura kin flew away.
2493.nuance: அடங்கி மனம் அடங்காத அசுரர் sets the sages' subdued mind against the asuras' unsubdued one in a single phrase, the nearest the narrative comes to saying what the asuras are. The vel is loosed by meditation on its point (தியானம் பண்ணி), not by the arm.

2494.reading: Flying off, the asuras took many forms and came back in ranks; looking well at the armies, mounting the firm peacock and standing clear, so that dharma might flourish he took form as the cause called gross, subtle and formless, ground the wicked asuras who kept coming to dust, and stood firm in tapas.
2494.nuance: தூல சூட்சம் அரூபமெனும் காரணம் names the three bodies, gross, subtle and causal, which the teaching later uses for the levels of the practice (2509, 2510). The war is fought with the same terms the instruction will use.

2495.reading: Seeing the victory he stood in, the sages doing tapas with upright minds, their minds cleared and glad, cherished and praised the feet of the forest-peacock hero, bowed their heads to his feet and gained the eye of grace; the ascetics and rishis bowed, beheld the vel-bearer standing firm, and each went to his own abode.
2495.nuance: சிலைகொண்டு நின்ற may mean standing like a hill, like an image, or with a bow; the sense is of a fixed, beheld form.

2496.reading: As they went seeking their abodes, the devoted great sage Agastya came; knowing the ordinance, he meditated on the victorious vel that was to destroy the asura kin, and said: knowing the goal, becoming subtle with the gross, taking the form of the gracious cause, knowing their treachery you destroyed them, Shanmuga, my guru, refuge.
2496.nuance: Agastya's praise already uses the work's technical pair, gross and subtle (தூலமுடன் சூட்சம்), so his question in 2498 is not naive: he asks for the inner meaning of an act he has described in those terms.

2497.reading: At the word 'refuge' the vel-bearer standing as Shanmuga looked at the great sage Agastya, knew his humility, and asked who he was; 'the child who worships your holy feet'; 'what inner instrument has come here? come with compassion', and giving his gracious glance he said that to help at the right moment is dharma, and asked him to tell with care how he had come.
2497.nuance: திரணமதாய் (as a straw) is read as humility, but the word is doubtful; கரணமந்தக் கரணம் plays on கரணம் (cause, instrument, the inner faculties) and its sense in the question is unclear. The exchange is the guru's testing of the disciple before teaching.

2498.reading: Asked to speak, Agastya full of light says to the peacock-hero: you destroyed the wicked asuras who came in a rush, with the vel, standing as Shanmuga; show the cause that stood as that holy form; tell as truth the cause of the inner form, gross and subtle.
2498.nuance: The hinge of the work: the disciple asks for the cause (காரணம்) behind the outer deed, and the second half answers with breath and mantra. ஆகார may be the Sanskrit akara (form) or the letter அ; உள்ளென்ற ஆகார தூல சூட்சம் is then 'the inner form, gross and subtle' or 'the gross and subtle of the inner A'.

2499.reading: Hearing the firm request, the peacock-hero affirmed it true and in order performed sacrifices; with observance he seated the great sage Agastya beside him, knowing the place, made the pit of Om, kindled fire with the mantra called the first, and knowing the fault, as the mantras were recited, the fullness came to be in the pot.
2499.nuance: ஓம் குண்டம் is a fire-pit that is Om, and the fullness arises in the கும்பம் (pot); tradition hears in these the body's fire and the retained breath (kumbaka), but the verse describes a rite. புரையறிந்து (knowing the fault or the hollow) is unclear.

2500.reading: Taking the pot that had become full, he anointed the great sage called truth, showed him the state of grace that is good for the nine planets, and the hill-like door of grace to be seen; with the mind gathered by knowledge, fix it with 'VINN'.
2500.nuance: The consecration (அபிடேகம்) from the pot of the rite begins the teaching proper. நவக்கிரகம் (nine planets) in the body is taken by tradition as the nine openings. விண்ணென்று ஊணே, the refrain of the teaching verses, is 'fix it saying VINN' or 'drive it to the sky'; both readings stand, and VINN may itself be a seed syllable.

2501.reading: With the force of 'VINN' within the tip of the tongue, the door of true knowledge opens; standing inside the way of that door, knowing the kala, looking at the lotus by the vaasi, fill at the root with 'VANG', and in firm samadhi let out with 'SING'; if you keep on this way always, hear the truth of the single tenfold initiation.
2501.nuance: The breath's phases are given seed syllables and places: VANG for inhalation (பூரி) at the root, SING for exhalation (ரேசி) in samadhi, and the tongue-tip (முனைநா) as the door, which tradition connects with the tongue turned back. தசதீட்சை (tenfold initiation) is announced but not listed.

2502.reading: Truly fixing 'VINN' in the suzhumunai, hear firmly the initiation that does not wear out: recite OM RING ANG UNG, and if you make sixteen repetitions with attention, Ganapati will shine gently; looking at yourself in the suzhumunai called the seat, if you subtly say OM NAMASIVAYA, the vision of Brahman comes before you look.
2502.nuance: Ganapati, placed at the root in 2489, is here what the seed letters make shine, so the legend's god is a stage of the practice. ஆராத தீட்சை (the initiation that is not cooled or worn) is uncertain. The verse promises Brahman-vision from the five letters alone.

2503.reading: Say NAMASIVAYANAMA, then VAYANAMASIVAYANAMASI; turn it head to foot and with care foot to head; say NAMASIVAYA SIVAYANAMA, and after that SIVAYANAMA SIVANAMA; say NAMASIVAYA and so change it: this is the siddhi of the true adhara.
2503.nuance: The practice is reversal (தலைகால் மாறி, head to foot) of the five letters, where Tirumular's is rotation. சிவநம has four letters and is probably a slip for சிவயநம. The exact strings are not recoverable from the printed text.

2504.reading: With mind on the five letters, son, properly changing them head to foot and foot to head, the deities of the adharas come purely and, as told, stand sweetly in the heart; meditating thus with devotion, firmly smearing ash as the ground, if you do this daily, the unstable gross body becomes stable.
2504.nuance: The promise is kaya-siddhi: the body that does not stay is made to stay by mantra, meditation and ash. ஆதார தேவதைகள் are the presiding deities of the adharas, who are said to take their stand in the heart rather than in their own centres.

2505.reading: Knowing the kala and standing in the state, hear with devotion the subtlety of the adharas: recite OM KILI ANG again and again; knowing the state recite ANG KILI NANG; recite VANG KILI SING, with compassion SING KILI VANG, VANG KILI YANG, and ANG KILI MANG.
2505.nuance: A table of bija strings, each a seed letter, கிலி and another seed letter. கிலி is itself a seed syllable in the Siddhars' mantra lore; which adhara each string serves is not said. The verse is a formula and is read here as such, not as a practice to follow.

2506.reading: After reciting, recite VANG KILI SING, truly ANG KILI SING, in order ANG KILI MANG, knowing the state MANG KILI RING, and from the first RING KILI OM; recite them changed head to foot; with light, fixing the mind's eye in the suzhumunai, purely wear the ash.
2506.nuance: The strings continue 2505 and are to be reversed as the five letters were in 2503; the series ends on OM. Only the setting is clear: the mind's eye in the suzhumunai and ash on the body.

2507.reading: Wearing the ash, sharply changing them foot to head, recite OM KILI RING, purely RING KILI MANG, MANG KILI SING; all the effects will appear in detail; recite MANG KILI (ING), and best one, SING KILI MANG.
2507.nuance: The strings of 2506 are run in the other direction (கால்தலையாய்). தோற்றும் செய்கை யாவும் promises that the effects (or the acts to be done) will show themselves. மங்கிலிங் has lost a syllable.

2508.reading: After reciting, recite VANG KILI SING, SING KILI MANG, in order MANG KILI NANG, knowing the state NANG KILI YANG, and with light MANG KILI OM; purely the twelvefold tapas is attained, the adhara called the street and the adhara above it; with the sky subsided and the eye subsided, stand established.
2508.nuance: ஈராறு தவம் (the twelve tapas) is not explained; it may be twelve years or twelve stations. வீதியென்ற ஆதாரம் (the adhara called the street) echoes Valmiki's middle street (2480) for the central channel; மேலாதாரம் is the centre above the six. The closing phrase, sky and eye subsided, is the refrain of 2509.

2509.reading: Stand with the eye subsided, fixing 'VINN', and if, knowing the state, you do pranayama, my son, the body is stone: where is Death? All the diseases called Death run away unseen; the vaasi becomes firm and the recited mantra is attained; I have told the gross with the subtle; hear now the compression of the gross that has shone.
2509.nuance: காலன் என்னும் வியாதி (the diseases called Death) makes Death a name for disease, and pranayama its cure; the claim is of a body made durable (கல், stone), not immortal in so many words. The verse closes the teaching's gross level and announces its summary.

2510.reading: Doing pranayama as told in the brief account of the adharas, gross and subtle, and with melting japa, tapas and puja truly seeing within yourself and becoming clear, abide in fullness, O living soul, and becoming the Supreme that stands as pranava, you too becoming it, go close into the cosmic void and with observance do pranayama with awareness.
2510.nuance: The soul (சீவான்மா) is told to become the Supreme (பரம்), with pranava as the form it takes; and the destination is அண்டவெளி, the cosmic void, within. Japa, tapas and puja are retained alongside pranayama, as in Valmiki's keeping of daily duty.

links.note: Tirumular derives Siva and Shakti, and then knowledge and action, from nada and bindu; this verse derives Parasiva, Shakti, the sevenfold creation and the two sons from the sound born of the Supreme.
Arunagiri names Murugan who circled the whole world on his golden peacock before the elephant-faced one and his father; here the contest is set and Murugan leaps on the peacock to round the hill.

Arunagiri praises Ganapati who won the fruit by circling his father; here Ganapati sees that Meru is the parents themselves, circles their feet and takes the mango. The Siddhar text adds the reasoning the hymn only names.
Arunagiri says Murugan taught Agastya the ways of knowledge and penance in Tamil at Palani; here Agastya hails Shanmuga as his guru and the rest of the work is that teaching.

Tirumular's Siva-guru makes the disciple bow, tests him with pure teaching and then shows the real and the unreal; Murugan asks Agastya who he is and why he has come before he teaches, and only then gives the gracious glance.

Romarishi gives inhalation, retention and exhalation their counts (four, four, one and three); this verse gives them seed syllables and places, VANG at the root to fill and SING in samadhi to let out. Two notations for the same phases.
Agasthiyar makes the suzhumunai the stream and names the Om-science of the letters; here, in the suzhumunai, Om with the seed letters and Om Namasivaya give the vision of Brahman.

Both permute the five letters as practice. Tirumular rotates them (SIVAYANAMA, MASIVAYANA, NAMASIVAYA and so on); Subramaniar reverses them head to foot and foot to head. The principle, that the mantra's power lies in its orders, is shared; the operation differs.

Tirumular: fix the mind twelve finger-breadths below the nose and the body never decays. Subramaniar: reverse the five letters, meditate, wear ash daily and the unstable gross body becomes stable. Both promise a body made to last by inner practice.

Tirumular: fill the ten nadis, hold prana and apana together, stay still, and there is no Yama for us. Subramaniar: fix the breath, do pranayama, and the diseases called Death run away. The same claim, with Death read as disease.

new_concepts.gloss: the central channel (sushumna) of the yogic body, between the left and right channels, in which the breath is made to rise
the breath as the Siddhars' practice: the in- and out-breath, coded as the sun and moon and as the horse, whose mastery is the way to siddhi

source_issues: 2500 has six lines where every other stanza of the work has eight; two lines are missing.
2503: சிவநம (four letters) in line 6 is probably a slip for சிவயநம; the permutation strings cannot be recovered exactly from the print.
2507: மங்கிலிங் in line 7 has lost a syllable (compare மங்கிலிசிங், மங்கிலிநங்).
2494: பந்திபந்தி யாங் is a broken sandhi for பந்திபந்தியாய்.
Several stanzas (2487, 2488, 2490, 2491, 2492, 2495, 2496, 2498, 2505, 2506, 2508) are printed with uneven line breaks, so the eight-line metre is not visible in the source.
